author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Two young New Hampshire cattle handlers turned years of practice into ribbons at the 2026 Hopkinton State Fair. Molly Potter and Rose DeFreitas showed four steers after learning to work with cattle together at a summer camp run by Miles Smith Farm in 2022.

Their preparation extended well beyond fair week. The pair worked with the animals through winter and spring, teaching them to walk calmly, respond to direction and remain composed around crowds. The calves came from Huckins Farm in Bristol, and the project required the students to build trust with animals much larger than they are.

Potter comes from a family with deep agricultural roots and is described as a 13th-generation farmer. DeFreitas developed her interest through the farm program and the partnership the two formed there. Their showing results reflected both technical handling and months of daily care. The experience also demonstrated how fairs connect young people with working agriculture: the ribbons are the visible result, but patience, safety and consistency are the skills developed long before an animal enters the ring.
dek: Molly Potter and Rose DeFreitas brought four steers to the 2026 fair after building their skills through farm camp and year-round training.
headline: Young handlers turn years of cattle training into Hopkinton Fair ribbons
